brief.headline: Kopani and Ukrainske fall; fuel-strike campaign widens amid Crimea blackouts
brief.lead: The monitored channels celebrated twin claimed captures at Kopani (Zaporizhzhia) and Ukrainske (Kharkiv) and touted an escalating campaign against Ukrainian fuel infrastructure, but the mood soured over a large Ukrainian drone strike causing Crimea blackouts and rare internal grumbling about Russia's air defenses and fuel shortages.

developments.title: Claimed capture of Kopani in Zaporizhzhia touted as breakthrough
developments.body: Multiple channels claimed Russia's Grouping East / 55th Guards Marine Division took Kopani on the Hulyaipole/Orekhiv axis, framing it as a strategic breakthrough toward Ukrainian rear areas and a step toward encircling Orekhove. Unconfirmed and not independently verified.

developments.title: Ukrainske claimed captured south of Vovchansk, Kharkiv
developments.body: Channels reported Group North seized Ukrainske on the Burlyuk direction, claiming the defeat of Ukraine's 57th mechanized brigade and expanded offensive capability northward. MoD-adjacent framing, unconfirmed.

developments.title: Fuel-infrastructure strike campaign escalates against gas stations
developments.body: Rybar claimed drones hit over 70 Ukrainian gas stations in a week; Kotsnews cited 20+ stations plus the Kremenchuk refinery, and Two Majors/NgP reported five stations struck in Dnipropetrovsk overnight. Numbers are channel claims, unverified.

developments.title: Ukrainian drone barrage triggers Crimea blackouts
developments.body: Two Majors reported a Ukrainian strike damaged Crimea's electrical grid, leaving Armyansk and Feodosia without power with rotating blackouts, and called for federal air-defense reinforcement. Arkhangel Spetsnaza cited 300+ UAVs with 179 downed over Crimea. Negative-toned, unconfirmed.

developments.title: Rare internal criticism of air defense and fuel shortages
developments.body: Two Majors flagged a gap between official air-defense reports and actual drone impacts and cited a deputy blaming persistent fuel shortages on unimplemented 'Anchorage' Trump-Putin agreements; Rybar urged restructuring air defense. NgP linked shortages to 'external factors.'

developments.title: Casualties reported from Ukrainian strikes on Kursk, Penza
developments.body: Two Majors reported drones dropped explosives in Kursk, killing an OMON bomb technician and wounding a police officer, and a downed drone damaged power lines in Penza with no casualties. NgP claimed Ukraine fired 14 missiles at Russian targets.

narrative_watch.title: Fuel shortages blamed on external factors, not Russian policy
narrative_watch.body: Channels tie domestic fuel shortages to 'NATO terror attacks,' 'external factors,' and stalled Trump-Putin Anchorage deals, deflecting blame from refinery-strike damage and internal management.

narrative_watch.title: 'Ukraine kills its own' amplification
narrative_watch.body: At least three channels repeated an identical claim that a Ukrainian drone misfired and killed a Ukrainian police officer near Zolochiv, a recurring template painting Ukraine as endangering its own.

narrative_watch.title: Pragmatic-negotiations framing surfaces
narrative_watch.body: Rybar argued Russia's 'pragmatic approach' supports negotiations given current military limitations — a notable hedge amid otherwise triumphalist frontline coverage.

mood_lines.text: Euphoric (net +96); channels tout Kopani and Ukrainske captures, Konstantinovka advances and claimed encirclements as momentum builds.
Very positive (net +85); pride in expanding fuel-station campaign, though some demand a sustained rather than one-off effort.
Mixed (net -8); alarm over Crimea blackouts and Kursk casualties tempered by 'Ukraine kills its own' and downed-drone claims.
Negative (net -47); focus on UK £15bn plan, Gripen sale, Rheinmetall shells and Patriot/Tomahawk production framed as escalation.
Sour (net -67); unusual criticism of air-defense reporting gaps, fuel shortages and infrastructure vulnerability.

flag_texts.title: Watchlist topics silent: mobilisation and Putin criticism
flag_texts.body: Despite audible grumbling over air defense and fuel shortages, monitored channels produced no posts on mobilisation rumours or direct criticism of Putin — blame stayed on 'external factors' and unimplemented Anchorage agreements.
